summary: Search the nine no-third pairs and three controls for a third in three places (surrounding, inside, bridge); three blind judges grade each candidate
logs: P01: NONE | P02: VARIABLE | P03: NONE | P04: NONE | P05: NONE | P06: VARIABLE | P07: FIXED | P08: FIXED | P09: FIXED | P10: VARIABLE | P11: NONE | P12: FIXED

table.third: The chirality of the environment: an achiral, parity-symmetric medium (vacuum, gas, achiral solvent, no chiral field).
The ambient field content: a single gravitational field with no composition-dependent coupling (the universality of free fall in the surrounding field).
The universe the complement is taken in: the one-bit Boolean algebra {0,1} (the word width and alphabet, with NOT as the complementing operation).
The vacuum and theory they are excitations of: a Lorentz- and CPT-invariant vacuum of the shared electron-positron field.

The shared interatomic distance matrix (the constitution plus bond geometry of the C-centred tetrahedron with H, F, Cl, Br). The only thing that differs between A and B is one bit, the handedness sign at the stereocentre.

The internal mass-energy budget of each body by interaction: constituent rest masses, nuclear binding, Coulomb energy and the neutron/proton imbalance. These differ strongly between Pt (Z=78, N/Z about 1.5) and Ti (Z=22, N/Z about 1.2).
N's self-copy: N contains a proper part in bijection with itself (the successor image {1,2,...}, or the evens). It is Dedekind-infiniteness read as internal structure.
The digit-position count (width = 1) of each bit string.
The shared vertex identification: the common labelling that makes vertex 1 of A the same vertex as vertex 1 of B, and so on.
The single Dirac electron field of which both are excitations (particle and antiparticle quanta), the one source of the mass parameter m and of the U(1) charge.
The shared data triple (constraint matrix = identity I2, bound vector b = (1,1), cost vector c = (1,1)) that both LPs are literally made of: the primal reads it by rows, the dual by columns.
The parity-invariant interaction law (the electromagnetic molecular Hamiltonian) that acts identically on both molecules.
The shared gravitational field (the common spacetime geometry), which couples universally to inertial energy-momentum regardless of composition.
The single Dirac electron-positron field, with CPT invariance of the underlying local, Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory.
LP strong duality: the transposed pairing of the shared data (constraint matrix I, right-hand sides (1,1), costs (1,1)), with weak duality sandwiching the optimum.

candidates.why: Disjointness and the union are fixed by the members of A and B alone. The only surrounding available is the universe {1..6}, and the stated relation already names it as the union, so naming it again would restate the relation.
candidates.vary_test: Enlarge the ambient universe to {1..10}. A and B are unchanged, they stay disjoint, and their union stays {1..6}, so the stated relation does not move. Only a 'complement' relation would depend on the universe, and that is not the stated one.

candidates.third: The chirality of the environment: an achiral, parity-symmetric medium (vacuum, gas, achiral solvent, no chiral field).
candidates.why: The mirror-image relation is intrinsic. 'Equal energies and boiling points' holds only because nothing in the surround distinguishes left from right, so a parity-symmetric environment maps one enantiomer onto the other.
candidates.vary_test: Keep A as exactly (R) and B as exactly (S) and put both in a chiral environment: a single-enantiomer solvent, a chiral stationary phase, circularly polarised light or a chiral crystal. The interactions become diastereomeric, so solvation energies and the volatility of each enantiomer from that solution differ, and the equality breaks. In an achiral environment it holds, apart from a tiny computed weak-interaction parity-violation energy.

candidates.why: The ratio of two numbers is intrinsic. The plausible surroundings (the transmitting medium, the observer's frame, the tuning standard) cannot reach it.
candidates.vary_test: Change the medium from air to helium: frequency is conserved, so only the wavelengths change. Change the observer's frame: a Doppler shift scales both frequencies by the same factor, so the ratio is unchanged. Retune the reference pitch from A4=440 to 432: the pair is still the stated 440 and 880 Hz. The ratio stays exactly 2 each time. Only whether the pair counts as an octave in a given tuning or hearing context could vary, and that is a different relation from the stated exact ratio.

candidates.why: Coprimality here is witnessed by the identity 3*12 - 35 = 1. It uses only integer arithmetic on A and B, so the ambient ring does not enter.
candidates.vary_test: Move the pair into Z[i], Q, or any ring that receives these integers. The identity still holds, so the ideal (35,12) is still the whole ring and they stay coprime. In a field the relation is trivially true. The relation survives every change of container.

candidates.why: B is defined as {A}, so membership is the definition of B and not a fact resting on a surround. The set-theoretic framework only hosts it.
candidates.vary_test: Any framework in which both objects exist and B = {A} (ZF, ZFC, non-well-founded set theory, a typed set theory) yields A in B. Varying the framework either keeps the relation or removes B, which redefines it.

candidates.third: The ambient field content: a single gravitational field with no composition-dependent coupling (the universality of free fall in the surrounding field).
candidates.why: The vacuum and the initial conditions are already fixed in the pair. What is not fixed is which fields act on the masses. Equal acceleration holds only because the only field acting couples to mass alone.
candidates.vary_test: Keep Pt and Ti, the same vacuum and the same initial conditions, and add a composition-dependent field to the surround. Candidates are a Yukawa fifth force coupling to baryon number or B-L (Pt and Ti differ in neutron excess), or a magnetic field gradient (they differ in susceptibility per unit mass). The accelerations then differ, so the relation changes. In a pure gravitational field it holds.

candidates.why: A bijection exists as an explicit formula (n -> n/2 for even n, -(n+1)/2 for odd n). It needs no choice, so the existence claim holds in every model of ZF and constructively.
candidates.vary_test: The only surround that matters is the category in which 'isomorphic' is read. Moving from Set to ordered sets or monoids turns 'bijection' into 'structure-preserving bijection', which is a different and false relation. That redefines the relation and does not vary a third, so there is no third to vary.

candidates.third: The universe the complement is taken in: the one-bit Boolean algebra {0,1} (the word width and alphabet, with NOT as the complementing operation).
candidates.why: 'Complement' is a relative notion and is not intrinsic to two symbols. It needs an ambient universe, and here it is the two-element alphabet that A and B jointly fill. Caveat: if 'binary 1' is read as the algebra's top element, the relation survives any width and there is no third.
candidates.vary_test: Take the same values 0 and 1 as numbers inside 8-bit words, or in a ternary alphabet. The bitwise complement of 00000000 is 11111111, not 00000001, so 0 and 1 are no longer complements and the relation fails. At one-bit width it holds.

candidates.why: The six vertex pairs, which are the edges of K4 on {1,2,3,4}, are named in the relation. The vertex set is also built into A ('on vertices {1,2,3,4}') and B ('the same vertices').
candidates.vary_test: Add a vertex 5 and there are ten pairs, so A and B no longer partition them. But then A and B are no longer graphs on exactly those vertices, which redefines both. Within the stated setup nothing in the surround can change.

candidates.third: The vacuum and theory they are excitations of: a Lorentz- and CPT-invariant vacuum of the shared electron-positron field.
candidates.why: Equal mass and opposite charge for a particle and its antiparticle follow from CPT invariance of the surrounding field theory. The relation rests on the symmetry of that frame and not on anything intrinsic to either particle taken alone.
candidates.vary_test: Keep an electron and a positron, but put them in a theory or vacuum with a CPT-odd Lorentz-violating background (for example a background vector coupling in the Standard-Model-Extension form). Their energy levels and effective masses then differ, so the equal-mass relation changes. This is counterfactual, since precision Penning-trap comparisons see no such difference.

candidates.why: 2 and 3 are the numerals S(S(0)) and S(S(S(0))) of the structure (N, 0, S). The successor relation is how B is built from A, so the structure is already inside the relation and not around it.
candidates.vary_test: Change the encoding (von Neumann, Zermelo, Church) or move to a non-standard model of Peano arithmetic. The objects called 2 and 3 change, but S(2) = 3 holds in each. Changing S itself redefines the stated relation.

candidates.why: The only inside content is the six elements, and those are A and B themselves. Disjointness and the union are element-by-element membership facts, so nothing is left over for a third to hold. The even/odd pattern is a description of the grouping, not a part the relation rests on.
candidates.vary_test: The parity rule can be dropped or redescribed (rename the six elements arbitrarily, keep the same memberships) and disjointness and the union stay exactly as they were. The only thing that changes the relation is an element, and swapping an element, for example putting 1 into A, redefines A.

candidates.third: The shared interatomic distance matrix (the constitution plus bond geometry of the C-centred tetrahedron with H, F, Cl, Br). The only thing that differs between A and B is one bit, the handedness sign at the stereocentre.
candidates.why: Mirror images share every interatomic distance. The electromagnetic energy and the intermolecular forces behind the boiling point depend on those distances, not on the handedness sign, so equal energies and boiling points follow. This is moderate, not strong: it is largely what 'mirror image' means. A footnote on the one inside piece that is not blind to the sign: parity-violating weak-interaction terms in the nuclei (growing steeply with nuclear charge, so Br matters) give a tiny real energy difference, so the stated equality holds only to that vanishing accuracy.
candidates.vary_test: With A and B exactly as stated the distance matrix cannot vary; changing it, for example swapping F for I, redefines both molecules. Flipping the handedness bit just swaps A and B, and the relation is unchanged. Changing the distances in only one enantiomer breaks both the mirror relation and the energy equality. Changing them in both together, for example an isotopologue, keeps the relation, so the relation rests on the distances being shared, not on their values.

candidates.why: A and B are bare numbers with a unit. The only inside structure is the factorisation, 440 = 2^3*5*11 and 880 = 2^4*5*11. The shared odd part 55 is real, but the relation is blind to its value; it contributes only sameness, which is the stated ratio restated at the level of parts. The unit (cycles per second) is shared and cancels in the ratio, so the relation does not rest on it either.
candidates.vary_test: Nothing inside can vary while 440 and 880 stay fixed. Varied jointly, the cofactor (456 and 912) or the unit (rad/s) leaves the ratio at exactly 2, so neither carries the relation. Varying either number alone redefines A or B.

candidates.why: The only parts are the prime factors, 35 = 5*7 and 12 = 2*2*3. Coprimality is exactly the statement that those two sets of parts do not overlap. The relation is the absence of a shared inside part, so there is nothing further inside for it to rest on. Bezout coefficients (-1 and 3) or Z/420 = Z/35 x Z/12 are consequences derived from the pair, not constituents of A or B.
candidates.vary_test: Changing any prime redefines A or B, for example 35 to 33 shares the factor 3 and gcd becomes 3. Re-expressing the same numbers (base, representation) leaves gcd = 1 unchanged, so no inside representation detail carries the relation.

candidates.why: A has no members, so it has no inside. B has exactly one member, and that member is A. The relation A is a member of B is B's entire internal structure (B = {A}), so no leftover part could be a separate third. The brace construction is the relation, not an addition to it.
candidates.vary_test: B's single member cannot vary without redefining B. For example B = {{empty set}} has a different member, and A is then not in B. A has nothing inside to vary.

candidates.third: The internal mass-energy budget of each body by interaction: constituent rest masses, nuclear binding, Coulomb energy and the neutron/proton imbalance. These differ strongly between Pt (Z=78, N/Z about 1.5) and Ti (Z=22, N/Z about 1.2).
candidates.why: Equal acceleration is a non-trivial statement only because the two budgets differ. It holds because each slice of the budget gravitates exactly as it resists acceleration. It is a real inside quantity with a measurable contrast, but the final step, that gravity is blind to the slices, is a law outside the bodies. That is why this is moderate and not strong.
candidates.vary_test: The budgets cannot vary with A and B as stated. Counterfactual: if one slice (say the Coulomb energy) gravitated with a weight shifted by a small epsilon relative to its inertia, Pt and Ti would accelerate differently by about epsilon times the difference in that slice's fraction, so the relation would change. Control: if A and B had identical budgets (Pt against Pt), the equality would hold trivially for any epsilon.

candidates.third: N's self-copy: N contains a proper part in bijection with itself (the successor image {1,2,...}, or the evens). It is Dedekind-infiniteness read as internal structure.
candidates.why: The bijection is built by splitting. Z = N plus a reflected second copy of N, and N absorbs a disjoint copy of itself (evens and odds). That is the inside reason the extra half of Z costs no cardinality. This is moderate: it is a property of A, not an independent object. Note the negative half of Z is not the third. It can be shrunk to finite or removed and the relation survives; what it rests on is A's self-absorbing infinity.
candidates.vary_test: It cannot vary without redefining A. Counterfactual: replace N by a finite set of k elements and the doubled set has 2k elements, so the equal-size relation fails. Changing which bijection is used (many exist) changes nothing, so the particular map is not the third.

candidates.third: The digit-position count (width = 1) of each bit string.
candidates.why: Bitwise complement is defined position by position over a fixed width. 0 and 1 are complements only because both occupy exactly one position. This is weak: the width is implied by the relation more than stated by A and B, and if A and B are read as abstract Boolean values with no digit positions the answer is none.
candidates.vary_test: Keep the values 0 and 1 but widen both to 8 positions: 00000000 and 00000001 are no longer complements, since the complement of 0 is 11111111. So the relation changes while the values stay as stated. Whether widening counts as redefining A and B is the ambiguity that makes this weak.

candidates.third: The shared vertex identification: the common labelling that makes vertex 1 of A the same vertex as vertex 1 of B, and so on.
candidates.why: Both graphs are paths (B is 3-1-4-2), so their isomorphism types are identical and give no hint of complementarity. The partition of the six pairs lives entirely in how the vertices of A line up with the vertices of B. It is a real inside structure (vertex identity), common to both and not part of either isomorphism type.
candidates.vary_test: Keep B a path on four vertices but relabel it. Of the 12 labelled copies of P4 on {1,2,3,4}, only the stated B has edge set exactly 13, 14, 24. For example, swapping labels 1 and 2 in B gives edges 23, 24, 14, which overlaps A on 23, so the partition fails. A as stated and B's isomorphism type are unchanged by this variation, while the relation breaks.

candidates.third: The single Dirac electron field of which both are excitations (particle and antiparticle quanta), the one source of the mass parameter m and of the U(1) charge.
candidates.why: The electron has no known sub-parts, so there is nothing else inside. Treated as quanta of one field, equal mass follows from one m and opposite charge from the antiparticle quantum carrying the reversed charge. This is borderline for the place: it is closer to the thing they are excitations of than to a part inside them. It is theory-laden, since CPT symmetry guarantees the oneness.
candidates.vary_test: It cannot vary with A and B as stated. Counterfactual: two independent fields with independent mass and charge parameters would allow unequal masses and non-opposite charges, so the relation would change. Varying m jointly in the one field keeps the relation, so the relation rests on the oneness of the field, not on its parameter values.

candidates.why: Under the Peano axioms 2 and 3 are primitive terms, S(S(0)) and S(S(S(0))), with no internal parts beyond the iteration chain. B containing A as its first two steps is just 'B is the successor of A' restated. Any set-theoretic encoding of the numbers (von Neumann 3 = 2 union {2}, or Zermelo 3 = {{{empty}}}) is an optional inside that varies freely.
candidates.vary_test: Switching the encoding changes everything inside A and B and leaves B = S(A) exactly intact, so no inside detail carries the relation. Changing the chain length redefines A or B.

candidates.third: The shared data triple (constraint matrix = identity I2, bound vector b = (1,1), cost vector c = (1,1)) that both LPs are literally made of: the primal reads it by rows, the dual by columns.
candidates.why: Both optimal values equal 2 because the two programmes are built from the same numbers. The equality rests on that coupling (strong duality applied to a feasible pair), and the value 2 rests on the entries of b and c. This is moderate: the dual is by construction the transpose reading of the same data.
candidates.vary_test: A and B cannot vary with the data fixed. Counterfactual: change the primal bound to x1 <= 2 and leave the dual untouched, and the values become 3 and 2, so equality breaks. Change b to (2,1) in both consistently and equality survives while the common value moves to 3. So the equality rests on the sharing, and the value 2 on the entries.

result.critic:
**1. Majority grades that look wrong or inconsistent**

- **P10 gets three grades for one object.** Inside (the Dirac field) is NONE, surrounding (the CPT-invariant vacuum/theory) is FIXED, and bridge (the Dirac field plus CPT) is VARIABLE. The surrounding and bridge candidates are almost the same, yet their majorities flip on 2-1 votes. You cannot vary the field while holding an electron and a positron fixed, because they are its excitations. So FIXED is the consistent grade for all three rows.
- **P10 bridge contradicts P12 bridge.** Strong duality is a theorem and got FIXED in P12. CPT is also a theorem, for local Lorentz-invariant field theory, so P10 bridge should not be VARIABLE.
- **P08 width gets two grades.** "Width = 1" as an inside candidate got NONE. The surrounding candidate, which explicitly includes "the word width", got a unanimous FIXED. By the rubric's own test, width is VARIABLE: keep the values 0 and 1, switch to 2-bit words, and NOT 00 = 11, which is not 01, so the relation breaks.
- **Context is graded by subject area, not by the test.** P02 surrounding (the medium) got VARIABLE and P08 surrounding (the universe the complement is taken in) got FIXED. Both pass "vary it with A and B fixed and the relation changes". The pattern looks like physics gets VARIABLE and math gets FIXED.
- **P06 surrounding is circular.** "Universality of free fall" restates "they fall with equal acceleration", so it should be flagged as a restatement rather than graded VARIABLE. P06 surrounding and P06 bridge are also the same candidate offered in two places.
- **P02 bridge is factually off.** The full Hamiltonian is not parity-invariant: the weak force gives the two enantiomers a tiny energy difference, so "equal energies" is only approximately true. None of the judges checked whether a candidate was true.
- **P07 inside FIXED is too strong.** Containing a copy of itself (being Dedekind-infinite) is necessary but not sufficient: the reals have that property too and are not in bijection with N. The candidate also describes only N, not Z.
- **Some NONEs are checker misses, not judgments:**
  - P01 and P09 have the same structure as P08 (a named universe split in two), but neither got a universe candidate. That would be {1..6} for P01 and the six pairs of the complete graph on four vertices for P09.
  - P01 has parity (n mod 2) as an obvious third.
  - P04 has the prime factorizations as an inside third: 35 uses {5, 7} and 12 uses {2, 3}, and coprime means those sets share no prime.

**2. Where the judges disagreed and why**

- **The split rows have a pattern.** Only 5 of the 15 real candidates split.
  - Opus is the lone dissenter in 4 of them (P06 bridge, P08 inside, P10 inside, P10 bridge), always toward FIXED.
  - Haiku dissents once (P10 surrounding, toward VARIABLE).
  - Sonnet contradicts itself: FIXED on P10 surrounding, VARIABLE on the nearly identical P10 bridge.
- **The first underlying question: where do laws of nature go?** The equivalence principle, CPT and parity invariance are neither fixed by definition nor something you can actually vary. The rubric has no slot for them, so judges force them into FIXED or VARIABLE.
- **The second underlying question: does a shared base count?** For things like the Dirac field or the word width, the judges disagree on whether the relation "rests on" them or whether they are only background. Opus reads "rests on" broadly; Sonnet and Haiku read it narrowly.
- **What that means for the majority.** The dissent is systematic, so the majority is not averaging out noise. It just encodes how Sonnet and Haiku read the rubric. A rule such as "theorem or law of nature goes to FIXED" or a separate LAW grade would remove most of the splits.

**3. What this test cannot show**

- **Whether the checkers miss real thirds.** 21 of the 36 rows had no candidate, and grading "none" as NONE is automatic. Headline unanimity is 31 of 36, but on real candidates it is 10 of 15. Whether a NONE is a true absence or a checker miss is untested (see P01, P04, P09), and only one model (Sonnet) proposed candidates.
- **Whether the grades are correct.** There are no reference answers, and three Anthropic models agreeing may share one bias. The judges did not check whether a candidate is true (P02 parity), sufficient (P07) or circular (P06, and arguably P12 bridge).
- **Whether the three places are distinct.** The same candidate shows up in two or three places (P06, P10, P12), so counting hits per place double-counts.
- **Whether the grades are stable.** This was one run with no repeats, so the 2-1 rows could flip.
- **Whether it transfers.**
  - These are 12 textbook pairs with clean answers, which says little about forced thirds in messy text such as replies.
  - There are no planted controls (a pair with a known real third and a pair with a known absent one), so false-positive and false-negative rates are unmeasured.
  - P06 inside, where a difference was offered as a third and correctly rejected, is the only near-control, and it is one data point.
